label: mid original phase, after early 0/f/d/c tokens, on a non-digit-like letter
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, at steps 3-7 (peak at 4-6), with a little at <DEL> and never in the copy phase or at t<2. It looks like it accumulates evidence: it is driven by how many tokens from a set S = {0,f,d,c, and more weakly 1,o,2,z} appeared earlier in the prefix, especially as the first token (first_tok f/0/d/c lift ~3.5-4.5x; prev2_tok 0 lift 4.8x). It fires on the current input when that input is not in S and is a first occurrence, and it prefers g, e, v, l, j, b (g lift 4.9x). The top activations are sequences like 0 f 0 l p [g] or d 0 o a [g] w. It does not fire on repeated tokens, on S tokens themselves, or late in long inputs. This looks like a graded linear sum, so no boolean predicate gets past F1 ~0.35 on dev. The simple rule given has dev P 0.27, R 0.47, mass recall 0.58. Larger magnitude goes with more early S tokens, especially 0/f at positions 0-2, and with g/e/v as the current input, but I only checked this qualitatively from the examples.
